name: application-folder-label-sidebar
title: Folder / Label Sidebar
description: Mail sidebar listing system folders (Inbox with an unread-count badge, Sent, Drafts, Archive) followed by a Labels group of colored, dot-marked labels.
useWhen: An email or messaging client needs a persistent sidebar to switch between system folders and user labels.
The active folder needs an unread count that's visually distinct from a decorative badge (Inbox's emphasized pill vs. Drafts' plain number).
Labels are user-defined and color-coded, distinct from the fixed system folder list above them.
avoidWhen: There's no folder/label concept — use settings-nav-list or side-menu for a general app sidebar instead.
You need nested/hierarchical labels — extend this with indented sub-items rather than a flat list.
The folder list is so long it needs its own search/filter — pair this with sidebar-search-filter above the list.
responsiveBehavior: The sidebar is a fixed w-56 column intended for a persistent mail-client rail; collapse or hide it below your chosen mobile breakpoint.
accessibility: The active folder carries aria-current="page", the correct token for identifying the current page in a navigation list.
The Inbox unread count uses a filled pill for visual emphasis, while less urgent counts (Drafts) use plain muted text — both remain real visible numbers, not color-only cues.
Label color dots are aria-hidden since the label's visible text name carries the same identifying information.

variants.title: Folder / label sidebar
variants.description: Four system folders (Inbox active with a 12-count badge, Sent, Drafts, Archive) plus three colored labels (Work, Personal, Urgent).
accessibility: Active-folder styling uses both background fill and font weight, not color alone.

variants.title: Folder / label sidebar (Dark)
variants.description: Folder/label sidebar adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Active background, count badge, and label-dot colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
